title: Wendell and the Scholarship
premise: Jonah Fairweather has survived fifteen years at Hollowmere Academy by being forgettable, hiding his gift for baking feelings into bread and his grief over his mother's disappearance. When the school's legendary ghost begins leaving him notes in ink that shouldn't exist — signed with his mother's handwriting — he's pulled into uncovering what the school board buried: a scholarship program that traded students' memories for endowments. With the help of Priya Chandrasekaran, the one person who remembers him too well, Jonah must expose the archive beneath the gymnasium before the last game of the season, when the board plans to 'renew' the scholarship and erase another class. He succeeds, but the price is the ghost — his mother's lingering memory — choosing to finally let go, leaving Jonah to bake bread that tastes of love instead of fear.
about_author: Wendell Zhou grew up above his family's bakery in a coastal town where fog was a daily character, and he still swears bread remembers things people don't. He writes young adult stories about quiet kids who discover that being seen is worth the cost.

chapters.title: The Careful Boy
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet Jonah working dawn shifts in the school-run bakery, kneading homesickness into rolls for scholarship students who never seem to remember eating them. He narrates his rules for invisibility. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety, cracked slightly when a roll comes out tasting of hope he doesn't feel.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A note appears inside his locker addressed 'Jonah Fairweather' — impossible, since no roster lists him that way — written in shimmering ink that fades from everyone else's eyes but his. The note says: 'You bake it true. Keep going.' Emotional beat: terror and a shameful thrill at being known.

chapters.title: Priya Remembers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya Chandrasekaran, the transfer student who inexplicably remembers every student the school forgets, confronts Jonah about the ghost notes. She reveals her own fragmentary memories of a brother the records say never enrolled. Emotional beat: two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Scholarship List
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Following the ghost's clues into the library's sealed annex, Jonah finds a ledger of 'Fairweather Scholars' dating back decades — each name crossed out, each crossed-out name belonging to someone no one can recall. His mother's name is on it, uncrossed. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Bread as Testimony
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya proposes using Jonah's gift as evidence: bread baked with recovered memories makes eaters briefly remember. They test it on a janitor, who weeps recalling a vanished friend. But Headmaster Voss tastes a crumb and smiles. Emotional beat: fragile hope shadowed by the sense they've been noticed.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The ghost leads Jonah through the tunnels beneath the gymnasium to a cold archive: jars of extracted memory-ink, contracts signed by grieving parents, and a recording of his mother refusing to surrender her final memory — of him. Emotional beat: grief transformed into fury; love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Headmaster Voss's POV. Voss offers Jonah a full scholarship — his mother's old seat — in exchange for the ledger and silence, framing the erasures as mercy for families drowning in debt. He genuinely believes it. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a kind face; Jonah almost says yes.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating Jonah/Priya POV. During the championship game, while the board convenes to renew the scholarship, Jonah and Priya smuggle memory-bread into the stands and the boardroom itself. Parents, alumni, and one wavering board member begin remembering names aloud. Emotional beat: rising chaos, courage, first open defiance.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Gymnasium
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cornered by Voss, Jonah is saved when the ghost manifests fully — his mother, sustained fifteen years by the one memory she refused to sell. She burns the archive's master contract with her remaining self, unraveling as she does. Emotional beat: climax; reunion and farewell in the same breath.

chapters.title: A Loaf Worth Remembering
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, epilogue weeks later. The scholarship is rebuilt honestly, named for the forgotten; Priya's brother's name is carved back onto the wall. Jonah bakes bread for the memorial that tastes openly of love and loss, and signs his name on the register for the first time. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — being seen, and surviving it.
